what: Boyd Gaming operates casinos. It runs properties in Las Vegas aimed at local residents rather than tourists, along with casinos in the American Midwest and South, and holds an online gaming business. It sold its stake in the sports betting company FanDuel in 2025.
customers: Regular casino customers, particularly Las Vegas residents who visit frequently, along with regional casino visitors across the Midwest and South, and online gaming customers.
money: Casinos serving Las Vegas residents, a repeat-visit business quite different from the Strip.
Online casino operations and management of tribal properties.
moat: Casino licences are granted by states in limited numbers, which makes an operating casino a protected asset in its local market. The Las Vegas locals business is the better part of the portfolio: residents visit frequently, spend predictably and do not depend on tourism, conventions or air travel, which is what makes Strip casinos volatile.
risks: Free cash flow was about negative $15.7M, reflecting capital spending on property improvements and the timing of the FanDuel proceeds.
The prior year’s figures are flattered by the gain on selling the FanDuel stake, so year-on-year comparisons overstate the decline in operations.
Debt of $2.7B against $354.2M of cash is substantial, which is normal for casinos but limits flexibility.
Casino spending is discretionary and falls when household budgets tighten, particularly at the regional properties.
Sixteen analysts average an $87.44 target, about 15% above the current price.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year, from $3.4B in 2021 to $4.1B in 2025.
The shares trade at about 11.2 times earnings, 7.6 times EV/EBITDA and 1.3 times sales.
The Las Vegas locals business is a repeat-visit model with far steadier economics than tourist-dependent Strip casinos.
State gaming licences are limited in number, which protects each property’s local market position.
The FanDuel sale produced a very large cash inflow, giving the company unusual flexibility for buybacks and debt reduction.
watch: Same-store revenue at the Las Vegas locals properties, and regional casino visitation. The locals business is the quality asset and the regional portfolio is the cyclical one.
view: Boyd Gaming’s best asset is the one people pay least attention to: casinos serving Las Vegas residents rather than visitors. The economics of that are entirely different from the Strip. A local plays regularly, spends predictably, and does not need an airline ticket, a convention or a holiday to show up. Strip casinos depend on air travel, group bookings and discretionary travel budgets, all of which disappear together in a downturn. The locals business is close to a consumer staple by casino standards.

Around that sit regional casinos across the Midwest and South, which are a more ordinary proposition — protected by limited state licences in each market, but dependent on discretionary spending from households whose budgets are not generous. That half of the portfolio is where a consumer slowdown shows up first, and it is the larger half by revenue.

The FanDuel sale in 2025 is important context for reading the numbers. Boyd held a stake in the sports betting business and sold it, producing a very large one-off gain that flatters the prior year’s earnings and makes year-on-year comparisons misleading. It also produced a great deal of cash and unusual balance sheet flexibility, which is being used for buybacks and debt reduction against $2.7 billion of borrowings. The negative free cash flow of $16 million is property capital spending and the timing of those flows rather than operating weakness.

At 11.2 times earnings and 7.6 times EV/EBITDA, this is priced as an ordinary leveraged casino operator, which undervalues the locals business and roughly fairly values the regional one. That seems like a reasonable asymmetry to me. What I would follow is same-store revenue at the Las Vegas locals properties specifically — it is the quality asset, it is where the durable economics are, and a consolidated revenue figure lets the cyclical half obscure it in both directions.
bull: The Las Vegas locals business delivers staple-like repeat revenue while FanDuel proceeds fund buybacks and debt reduction, and 7.6 times EV/EBITDA undervalues the mix.
bear: Discretionary spending weakens at the regional casinos that are the larger half of revenue, and $2.7 billion of debt amplifies the earnings decline.
